errors: No mathematical content on this page, so no mathematical errors.

results.what: Programme of defining differentiation/integration of arbitrary (non-integer) order ν, consistent with derivatives (ν>0 integer), iterated integrals (ν<0 integer) and the identity (ν=0)
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz (1695 question), Euler, Lacroix, Fourier, Abel (1823), Liouville (1832–37); Riemann (1847, publ. 1876); the integral operator is named Riemann–Liouville

deep.surprise_reason: This is the first page of a well-known Riemann manuscript. It was published in his Gesammelte Werke (1876) and is the origin of the name 'Riemann–Liouville integral'. The page itself is introductory prose only.

checkable.asserts: The power rule for D^a x^m reduces to the ordinary derivative at a=1 (simplifies to 0).
At order a=-1 the same formula gives the ordinary integral from 0 (simplifies to 0).
At order 0 the operator is the identity (simplifies to 0).
The Riemann–Liouville half-integral of x from 0 equals 4 x^(3/2)/(3 sqrt(pi)), with x>0 (result 0).

transcription_corrections: Marginal note likely reads '(Note auf beiliegenden Zettel)' rather than 'beiliegendem'; the meaning is the same.
The heading 'XIX' (pencil, boxed, possibly overwritten) corresponds to number XIX in the Gesammelte Werke.
The '2' in the right margin next to line 6 and at the bottom is an archival/page-sequence mark, not part of the text.
